Investor Relations ABOUT INVESTORS CORPORATE GOVERNANCE DarGlobal Today DarGlobal PLC is an international real estate developer specializing in exclusive luxury developments across the world’s most coveted cosmopolitan cities. Catering to global citizens seeking prime investments, second homes, and luxury living, DarGlobal transforms real estate into economic catalysts, unlocking opportunities for both investors and the countries it enters. DarGlobal has partnered with over 11 world-renowned luxury brands, including Trump Organization, Aston Martin, Automobili Lamborghini, ELIE SAAB, Marriott Residences, Missoni, Mouawad, Fendi, Pagani Automobili, Paramount and W Hotels. These collaborations offer unique investment opportunities in global cities, providing both wealth growth and protection. Listed on the London Stock Exchange, DarGlobal goes beyond property development; it drives economic transformation by attracting international clients and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). With a presence in 13 international cities across 8 countries, DarGlobal’s portfolio spans the United Kingdom, Spain, Greece, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Oman, the United States, and Qatar. The company is also expanding into world-class hospitality, developing luxury hotels in Dubai, Muscat, Riyadh and Jeddah.

Les Vagues is developed by DarGlobal in partnership with Qetaifan Projects and ELIE SAAB, marking the first co-branded residences on Qatar's Qetaifan Island North. Where is Les Vagues located? Les Vagues sits on Qetaifan Island North in Lusail, Qatar, with views of the sea, marina and Lusail skyline. What types of residences are available at Les Vagues? The performance was driven by the Group’s projects and sustained demand across its diversified portfolio in the GCC, Europe, and the UK. Growth was primarily anchored by revenue recognition from landmark projects, including The Astera, Interiors by Aston Martin and Neptune, Interiors by Mouawad. Entry into financial services via DIFC In a move that diversifies the Group’s operations, Dar Global is acquiring a licensed financial services company in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC). It will also equip Dar Global with the ability to create and manage investment vehicles that attract institutional and private capital from the GCC and beyond, enabling participation in larger‑scale projects in a capital efficient manner.

Dar Global, the luxury international real estate developer, started trading on the London Stock Exchange (LSE) on February 28, and became one of the first Saudi homegrown brands to list on the LSE’s main market. Ziad El Chaar, CEO of Dar Global, says: “We have seen a lot of encouragement from the Ministry of Investment in Saudi Arabia to spread brands overseas. Our initial public offering (IPO) definitely created a lot of news … so many more companies may consider this route.” Dar Global was established as the international development subsidiary of the Dar Al Arkan Real Estate Development Company, which listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange in 2007. The restructuring process to set up a separate company took almost 10 months. However, Mr El Chaar says preparing for the transaction was a straightforward process as the parent company is already public and has a high

However, Mr El Chaar says preparing for the transaction was a straightforward process as the parent company is already public and has a high degree of governance. Dar Global aspires to become a top-50 developer globally, outside China, and therefore desired to go public on one of the biggest international stock markets. As Mr El Chaar explains, Dar Global wanted the high profile of a London listing and to be subject to English law, which encourages future investment and growth in one of the biggest international property markets. “We understand the value of joint ventures to expand internationally, and they need development agreements under international laws and a structure that facilitates institutional funding,” he says. Why big fashion brands are building houses in Marbella (press release, 2023-09-24)
to see if the association with a big luxury design brand can help to sell five-star properties in four-star areas,” he says. Others brands roll up their designer sleeves and get stuck in. “Domenico [Dolce] was interested from day one,” Rodriguez says of the D&G scheme. “Buyers can see there are two real people behind this project, Domenico and Stefano [Gabbana], and they can see they are personally involved — which is something that buyers are willing to pay for.” From the brand’s point of view, entrusting a property developer to turn the essence of its multibillion-pound company, whose reputation has been honed over decades, into bricks and mortar comes at a risk. “The location is crucial and this is one of the best areas in Spain. But we made sure we didn’t rush into choosing a developer. We need to be very careful as we need to protect the asset,” says Alfonso Dolce, Domenico’s younger brother and the company’s chief executive, who has been visiting Marbella for 23 years.

Alfonso adds that D&G and Sierra Blanca Estates, which has been building on the coast since 1985 (the same year, coincidentally, that the fashion house launched), share a deep bond. “We are both family-run companies, and we share two important things: family and passion,” he says. With the Marbella project, he adds, “we are giving a whole lifestyle, not just a building. We don’t need to sell fast.” For the super-rich keen for the ego boost — and potential profit — that comes with being one of the first buyers, that message may fall on deaf ears. title: Missoni and Dar Global launch residential development project in southern Spain
text:

title: Five Types of Insurance Coverage Every Homeowner Needs
text:
Five Types of Insurance Coverage Every Homeowner Needs (blog article)
Five Types of Insurance Coverage Every Homeowner Needs Owning a home is a significant achievement and a substantial investment that necessitates protection. As a homeowner, it’s crucial to understand the various types of insurance coverage available to safeguard your property and finances. Here are five essential types of insurance coverage every homeowner should consider: 1. Homeowners Insurance This is the most fundamental and necessary form of insurance for homeowners. It covers the structure of your home, your personal belongings, and liability protection in case someone is injured on your property. Homeowners insurance typically covers damage from fires, storms, theft, and other common hazards. However, it’s important to read the fine print, as certain natural disasters like floods and earthquakes are often not covered. 2. Flood Insurance Standard homeowners insurance policies do not cover flood damage. If your home is in a flood-prone area, flood insurance is indispensable. This insurance covers damage to your home’s structure and belongings due to flooding. The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and private insurers provide

title: Five Types of Insurance Coverage Every Homeowner Needs
text:
Five Types of Insurance Coverage Every Homeowner Needs (blog article)
a flood-prone area, flood insurance is indispensable. This insurance covers damage to your home’s structure and belongings due to flooding. The National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and private insurers provide this coverage, which can be a lifesaver in safeguarding your investment against unpredictable natural disasters. 3. Earthquake Insurance Similar to flood insurance, earthquake insurance is a must-have if you live in an area prone to earthquakes. This coverage helps repair or rebuild your home and replace personal belongings in the event of an earthquake. Considering the devastating impact an earthquake can have, this insurance provides essential financial protection. 4. Umbrella Liability Insurance Umbrella liability insurance provides additional liability coverage beyond what your standard homeowners insurance offers. It protects your assets and future earnings in case you’re sued for damages that exceed the liability limits of your other insurance policies. It’s particularly valuable for homeowners with significant assets or potential exposure to liability claims. 5. Home Warranty or Home Repair Insurance While not traditional insurance, a home warranty or home repair

Home Warranty or Home Repair Insurance While not traditional insurance, a home warranty or home repair insurance can be a wise investment. This coverage typically pays for the repair or replacement of major home systems and appliances that break down over time. It’s a practical way to manage unexpected repair costs and ensure that your home remains in good working order. In summary, while homeownership is a source of pride, it also comes with risks.
